description:
`Shortened<C>`'s systematic restriction encodes by writing the message into a mother-length buffer and encoding through the mother, and `encode_into` allocates two mother-length buffers per call (about 16 KB per normal-frame DVB-T2 encode). The wrapper has no reusable-workspace or allocation-free single-encode path.

## Background

Surfaced by the DVB-T2 cutover (`@/issue/97410c80`): the DVB-T2 outer encoder is `Shortened<DvbT2MotherCode>` through this path, and the survey's W1 throughput cells for the DVB-T2 rows measure it. The mother's own encoders expose allocation-free single and reusable-workspace batch methods (`@/issue/ae03bcd0/requirement/REQ-07`); the wrapper does not forward them.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `Shortened<C>` exposes an allocation-free single-encode path with a caller-held workspace, and a reusable-workspace batch path, both equal to `encode` on every shared fixture and covered by the shared conformance cases.
- [hard] REQ-02: The DVB-T2 W1 cells encode through the workspace path with no per-call allocation, evidenced by the allocation-count test pattern the crate already uses.
title: Shortened<C> systematic restriction lacks an allocation-free encode path
